title: docs: define parallel Vast canary coordination
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Defines one atomic canary lease per production GPU slot
- Allows one scheduled run to prepare multiple unlocked targets in parallel
- Keeps volatile thresholds, budgets, and temporary machine cooldowns in the scheduled task
- Removes transient machine exclusions from the fleet inventory
- Keeps promotion human-approved and serialized per workload

Checks: skill validator; `git diff --check`; live automation policy assertions

gist.headline: Canaries get their own nests
gist.blurb: The Vast fleet playbook now gives every production GPU slot its own atomic canary lease. Several unlocked targets can prepare together, while human-approved promotions stay politely single-file.
gist.summary: Documented per-production-slot atomic canary leases for Vast GPU operations, allowing scheduled runs to prepare multiple unlocked targets in parallel while keeping promotion human-approved and serialized per workload.
gist.impact: Fleet operators gain clearer coordination rules: parallel preparation is safe across unlocked GPU targets, while volatile thresholds, budgets, cooldowns, and final promotions remain controlled in the scheduled workflow.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy GPU garden with several separate canary nests beside retro server plants: Polli, wearing a tiny operations headset, places individual lease tags on each nest while multiple code-plants are prepared in parallel. A calm human approval gate and a single orderly path to a blooming production flower represent serialized promotion.
